idiom_name: nested public key class with a private constructor inside the authorised collaborator (private access is scoped to the top-level class body)
implementation_notes: Java has no friend declaration, but a private member or constructor is accessible within the body of the top-level class that encloses its declaration (JLS 6.6.1), and that scope includes nested types: a nested class's private constructor can be called from anywhere inside its top-level class and from nowhere else, while another top-level class is rejected. The key therefore has to be nested inside the authorised collaborator, not inside the restricted type - the opposite of the C++ nesting habits - and the grant is exactly one class. The restricted operation stays public or package-private and simply requires the key type; keys are ordinary objects, so the collaborator can delegate one deliberately. When the grantee is a module rather than a class, a qualified export in module-info (JEP 261) is the larger-grained alternative.
pitfalls: Nesting the key in the restricted type does not work: that class is a different top-level class and cannot call the key's private constructor.
A key nested in the authorised collaborator becomes part of its public API, so moving or renaming the collaborator changes every restricted signature.
Package-private or protected constructors widen the grant to the package or to subclasses; keep the constructor private and the key class final.
